structure.heading: Attrition-Risk Role Identification and Recommended Salary Band and Equity Corrections
text_content: **Attrition-Risk Role Identification and Recommended Salary Band and Equity Corrections**

The attrition-risk identification criteria applied in this study designate roles as at risk when an incumbent compa-ratio is below 0.90 and the role’s trailing 12-month voluntary attrition equals or exceeds 15%. This threshold was applied to payroll and HRIS data as of March 31, 2026, across North America and EMEA populations. The approach aligns with Total Rewards practices at peer firms and informs which job families warrant urgent band and equity review to mitigate turnover and maintain operational continuity effectively.

The study identifies 9 roles that meet the attrition-risk threshold; notable examples include Software Engineer II and Senior Data Analyst. Other impacted titles span Customer Support Lead, Product Manager II, and two specialist roles within Marketing and Finance. Flags were concentrated in high-growth product lines and customer-facing operations during Q4 2025 through Q1 2026. Human Resources and Hiring Managers were notified on April 15, 2026, to prioritize retention strategies and targeted compensation interventions and reporting.

Recommended actions prioritize immediate band adjustments and equity corrections. For Software Engineer II we recommend increasing the salary band midpoint by 6% effective June 1, 2026; for Customer Support Lead the recommendation includes equity adjustments of $3,500 per impacted employee, to be processed in the June payroll cycle. Implementation governance should involve Compensation, Legal, and Finance with a program review on September 30, 2026, to measure attrition and internal equity outcomes regularly.

sections.heading: Study Scope and Data Sources
sections.body: This benchmarking review compares the organization’s FY2025 pay bands against aggregated market data from the Radford Technology Survey (Q4 2025 cut) and the National Industry Remuneration Index (NIRI 2025). The analysis covers 64 benchmarked roles across Engineering, Product, Commercial, Corporate Services, and Operations. Market positioning was assessed at the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles, with geographic differentials applied for London, Manchester, and Remote-UK profiles. All compensation figures reflect base salary only, excluding variable incentives and long-term equity.

sections.heading: Overall Market Positioning
sections.body: Across the full population, the organization’s salary midpoints sit at approximately the 43rd percentile of the market, with notable dispersion by function. Engineering roles are most compressed, averaging 11% below market median at midpoint, while Corporate Services roles are broadly aligned at 98% of market median. Commercial leadership roles exceed market median by 6%, largely driven by historical retention adjustments. Band width variance is generally consistent (±15%), though several legacy bands exhibit structural midpoint drift relative to current market rates.

sections.heading: Attrition Risk Roles
sections.body: Three role families demonstrate elevated attrition risk due to sustained sub-market positioning and external hiring pressure: Senior Backend Engineers (Band E4), Data Engineers (Band E5), and Product Designers (Band P3). For Senior Backend Engineers, current midpoint salary (£82,500) trails the market median (£92,000) by 10.3%, with voluntary attrition at 18% over the past 12 months compared to a company average of 11%. Data Engineers show the largest gap at 13.7% below median, compounded by aggressive counteroffers in the London market. Exit interviews consistently cite external base pay increases between 15–22% as primary drivers.

sections.heading: Recommended Band Adjustments
sections.body: It is recommended that Band E4 and E5 midpoints be increased by 8% and 10% respectively, with corresponding range adjustments to preserve band integrity. Product Design Band P3 should receive a 6% midpoint uplift to restore alignment to at least the 50th percentile of the NIRI survey. These adjustments would impact 37 incumbents and are projected to increase annualized base payroll by £1.14 million, representing a 2.6% increase to total fixed compensation cost. Phasing adjustments over two quarters is advised to mitigate budget concentration in a single fiscal period.

sections.heading: Equity and Compression Corrections
sections.body: Beyond structural band updates, individual equity corrections are required for 19 incumbents currently paid below 90% of revised band midpoint. Particular attention is required for high-tenure engineers whose pay progression has not kept pace with external market acceleration, resulting in internal compression versus new hires. Targeted adjustments averaging 7.5% are recommended to restore internal equity and reduce flight risk. Future governance should include semi-annual market reviews for critical technical roles to prevent recurrence of midpoint lag.

structure.full_text:
Compensation Benchmarking Review — Market Alignment and Risk Assessment
Ref: CBR-27-2026 | Date: 12 February 2026 | Prepared by: Total Rewards & Analytics

Section Study Scope and Data Sources
This benchmarking review compares the organization’s FY2025 pay bands against aggregated market data from the Radford Technology Survey (Q4 2025 cut) and the National Industry Remuneration Index (NIRI 2025). The analysis covers 64 benchmarked roles across Engineering, Product, Commercial, Corporate Services, and Operations. Market positioning was assessed at the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles, with geographic differentials applied for London, Manchester, and Remote-UK profiles. All compensation figures reflect base salary only, excluding variable incentives and long-term equity.

Section Overall Market Positioning
Across the full population, the organization’s salary midpoints sit at approximately the 43rd percentile of the market, with notable dispersion by function. Engineering roles are most compressed, averaging 11% below market median at midpoint, while Corporate Services roles are broadly aligned at 98% of market median. Commercial leadership roles exceed market median by 6%, largely driven by historical retention adjustments. Band width variance is generally consistent (±15%), though several legacy bands exhibit structural midpoint drift relative to current market rates.

Section Attrition Risk Roles
Three role families demonstrate elevated attrition risk due to sustained sub-market positioning and external hiring pressure: Senior Backend Engineers (Band E4), Data Engineers (Band E5), and Product Designers (Band P3). For Senior Backend Engineers, current midpoint salary (£82,500) trails the market median (£92,000) by 10.3%, with voluntary attrition at 18% over the past 12 months compared to a company average of 11%. Data Engineers show the largest gap at 13.7% below median, compounded by aggressive counteroffers in the London market. Exit interviews consistently cite external base pay increases between 15–22% as primary drivers.

Section Recommended Band Adjustments
It is recommended that Band E4 and E5 midpoints be increased by 8% and 10% respectively, with corresponding range adjustments to preserve band integrity. Product Design Band P3 should receive a 6% midpoint uplift to restore alignment to at least the 50th percentile of the NIRI survey. These adjustments would impact 37 incumbents and are projected to increase annualized base payroll by £1.14 million, representing a 2.6% increase to total fixed compensation cost. Phasing adjustments over two quarters is advised to mitigate budget concentration in a single fiscal period.

Section Equity and Compression Corrections
Beyond structural band updates, individual equity corrections are required for 19 incumbents currently paid below 90% of revised band midpoint. Particular attention is required for high-tenure engineers whose pay progression has not kept pace with external market acceleration, resulting in internal compression versus new hires. Targeted adjustments averaging 7.5% are recommended to restore internal equity and reduce flight risk. Future governance should include semi-annual market reviews for critical technical roles to prevent recurrence of midpoint lag.

FY2026 Compensation Benchmarking Review – Market Alignment Analysis
Ref: CB-26-041 | Date: 18 February 2026 | Prepared by: Total Rewards & Workforce Analytics

Section Study Scope and Data Sources
This benchmarking review evaluates current pay bands across 27 core roles against 2025–2026 market survey data sourced from Mercer TechComp, Radford Global Technology Survey, and the Midwest Manufacturing Consortium survey. Market medians were normalized to a 50th percentile national composite and adjusted for our primary operating geographies (Illinois, Texas, and North Carolina). Internal data reflects active employee base as of 31 December 2025. The objective is to quantify variance from market and identify roles where misalignment may elevate attrition exposure.

Section Overall Market Positioning
Across all benchmarked roles, base salary midpoint positioning averages 94.2% of market median, with wider dispersion in technical and revenue-generating functions. Administrative and finance roles are generally within ±3% of market, while engineering and cybersecurity positions trail by 8–14% at midpoint. Notably, the Senior Software Engineer band (P4) is positioned at 88% of market median, with compa-ratios clustering below 0.92. Variable pay opportunities remain competitive; however, base salary compression is evident in mid-career levels.

Section Roles with Elevated Attrition Risk
Voluntary turnover for 2025 reached 17.6% in Data Engineering and 19.3% in Cloud Infrastructure, compared to a company-wide average of 11.4%. Exit interview data indicates compensation as a primary or contributing factor in 61% of these cases. The Cybersecurity Analyst III role shows a 12% lag to market median and has experienced three regretted losses in Q4 alone. Sales Engineering positions, while only 5% below market at midpoint, face aggressive external recruiting pressure with sign-on premiums averaging $18,000 above our current offers.

Section Recommended Band Adjustments and Equity Corrections
We recommend increasing midpoint values for P3–P5 Engineering bands by 6% effective 1 July 2026, with a targeted equity adjustment pool of $1.8M to bring incumbents to at least 95% compa-ratio relative to revised midpoints. Cybersecurity and Cloud Infrastructure bands should receive a 9% midpoint adjustment to restore alignment to the 50th percentile market reference. For Sales Engineering, we advise maintaining current band structure but implementing a targeted retention allocation of $450,000 focused on high performers below 1.0 compa-ratio. Total estimated annualized cost impact is $3.2M, representing 1.7% of current payroll, which can be phased over two quarters to manage budget absorption.

Section Cost Control and Governance Measures
To balance competitiveness with fiscal discipline, adjustments will prioritize critical-skill roles and incumbents with strong performance ratings (Exceeds or Above Expectations). Future annual review cycles will adopt a formal market trigger threshold of ±5% from composite median before structural band changes are recommended. Quarterly market pulse checks will be conducted for high-volatility roles such as AI Engineering and Cybersecurity. These controls are intended to prevent future drift while sustaining a defensible pay-for-performance framework.
